\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\vspace{-2pt}

\paragraph{Limitations.}\looseness=-1
Our conclusions rest on $N{=}2$ VLM-to-VLA transitions plus one VLA-to-VLA case, all causal decoders on a single benchmark (LIBERO); flow-matching~\cite{black2024_pi0} and diffusion~\cite{ghosh2024_octo} heads may differ.
All findings are correlational ($R^2$ measures decodability, not causal reliance); the $\Delta R^2$--success-rate correlation ($\rho{=}0.583$, $p{=}0.10$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}) is underpowered ($n{=}9$); each architecture uses a single checkpoint; and the three-tier gradient has $n{=}1$ at Tier~2.
All evaluations are open-loop---we measure representational geometry on offline demonstrations without closing the loop through simulated or real execution---so the link between $\Delta R^2$ and downstream task performance remains indirect.

\paragraph{Practical implications.}\looseness=-1
The trained/reference decomposition suggests actionable guidelines for VLA development.
$\Delta R^2 > 0.10$ serves as a lightweight diagnostic: a VLA whose exit-layer $R^2$ drops well below its mid-layer peak likely under-utilizes its own learned representations, and this gap can be detected with linear probes alone, without closed-loop rollouts.
Because action-relevant structure peaks at intermediate layers rather than the exit, downstream modules such as reward models or planners should tap mid-layer features instead of the final hidden state.
The observation that instruction sensitivity is distributed across L1 heads---rather than concentrated in a sparse subset---implies that aggressive early-layer pruning risks degrading instruction following even when individual per-head ablation effects appear modest.

\paragraph{Conclusion.}\looseness=-1
We present the first cross-architecture analysis of instruction routing in VLAs, decomposing observed phenomena into training-associated effects (exit collapse, counterfactual sensitivity) and inherited backbone properties (L1 attention routing) across three architecture families and four task suites.
Extending this framework to diffusion-based action heads, encoder-decoder VLAs, and closed-loop evaluation are natural next steps toward a comprehensive mechanistic account of vision-language-action fine-tuning.
